summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type II diabetes, cardiomyopathy due to Chagas disease, and a history of coronary artery bypass grafting presented after a fall attributed to profound weakness. He was found to have severe hyperkalemia (potassium 8.7) at an outside hospital, with EKG changes including bradycardia and QRS widening. He received emergency treatment with calcium gluconate, insulin, bicarbonate, and kayexylate, followed by urgent hemodialysis, which normalized his potassium level. His symptoms improved, and he was transferred to the medical floor for monitoring. A nutrition consult educated him and his wife on a low-potassium renal diet to prevent recurrence. CT imaging confirmed no intracranial or cervical spine injury from the fall. He was discharged home with home services, on adjusted medications including reduced carvedilol and pravastatin, with stable vital signs and laboratory values.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Fall from other slipping, tripping, or stumbling
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
Carrier or suspected carrier of Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus
